doc.title: Ingrid Sertso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Woodstock, New York, August 11, 2014

title: Adoring Chet Baker; brother Klaus; wanting to be a dancer
summary: Chet Baker's singing brought her to music; her brother Klaus drummed in his European rhythm section and quit over his drug use; she once wanted to dance.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Yeah. Wow. Yeah, that’s a pretty interesting experience right there. What was it that you liked about Chet Baker?

Oh, I adore him. Because he sang like he played. I totally adored him. My father was a professor so whenever we came home early from school, my brother Klaus and me — Klaus played drums in my room and I sang. And we had a Chet Baker record going. And I just loved the softness of his voice. He loved the way he phrased. I loved the songs that he sang, [sings] “Time After Time” [scats]. The warmth of his voice, very relaxed, and the way he phrased. Chet Baker couldn’t sit and read one note. Chet Baker couldn’t read one note of music. He had such a musicality. He never read music. And then Klaus, my brother, that lives now in Italy on the Island of Elba became a drummer, a European drummer in the European rhythm section of Chet Baker. So he was lucky you know. I only met him once in Manhattan when he was already almost totally gone you know. But he was lucky and he really loved to play with him — a lot in France and in Spain and in Germany. And then he quit with him and I said, “How can you quit with Chet Baker?” And he said, “Well in the intermission I had to go with him to the bathroom to find another place where he can stick the needle.” And it was so depressing because he was

such a cool guy you know, that he quit. It was just the way he played. He must have been also, when he wasn’t on drugs, a great guy. I heard him say on some weird tape, some announcements to the audience you know, “You’d better listen.” You know, talk about listening, very intelligent, very beautiful. But the drugs killed him. And that brought me to music, Chet Baker’s singing brought me to music. So I always wanted to be a dancer, and my parents sometimes had the money, sometimes didn’t have it. And dance you have to do from morning 9:00 to 5:00 in the evening, or 8:00 in the evening you know, to keep that body flexible. And in this society, in the West, you have to go through the whole ballet training in order to become a modern dancer, hip hop dancer, whatever, jazz dancer. But I wanted something with music and that’s —
Yeah. I always feel sorry for dancers too because by the time you’re 30, you’re like — then you’re going to have to become a teacher you know.
Yeah. Now it goes up to 45.
Because of the health awareness and everything. I met people, you can actually put 15 years off the age they are in.
